weight_size_estimates_GB_decimal.method: Approximate parameter_count × bytes per parameter: BF16/FP16 2 bytes, INT8 1 byte, 4-bit approximately 0.6 byte including rough scales/metadata. Excludes runtime memory, tokenizer/config files, and training optimizer/activation states.

classification_notes.A_foundation_candidates: SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, OLMo-1B-hf, Pythia-70M/160M/410M/1B/1.4B/2.8B. All have a documented pretrained lineage and downloadable weight files. Qwen2.5-3B is technically a foundation checkpoint but stays in D due to the posted research license.
classification_notes.B_strong_but_derived: Instruction/chat variants are explicitly excluded from foundation rankings. Examples: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-*-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen2.5-*-Instruct, apple/OpenELM-*-Instruct. They derive from corresponding base checkpoints and should not be substituted for the base files when continuing pretraining.
classification_notes.C_deployment_only_not_foundation: GGUF and other quantized artifacts are deployment conversions, not the native pretrained starting weights in this dataset. Prefer the native Safetensors/original training checkpoint for training. No quantized-only repository is promoted as a foundation candidate.
classification_notes.D_license_access_problem: OpenELM family is research-only under the current license. Qwen2.5-3B repository LICENSE is non-commercial Qwen Research License despite conflicting/changed HF badge history. MobileLLM-125M was also identified but carries Meta FAIR Noncommercial Research License and is omitted from foundation shortlist for commercial Pocket AI pending legal review. All shortlisted repositories are non-gated based on their public Hub pages; authentication is not required to access public files, though normal HF client rate limits may apply.

tier_shortlist.~100M: Pythia-70M for transparent controlled experiments; SmolLM2-135M for a newer, more capable small starting point and more current training corpus. Neither is genuinely a 100M model; they are nearest useful checkpoints.
tier_shortlist.~300M: SmolLM2-360M offers Apache-2.0 and a published recipe/data description; OpenELM-270M is technically interesting but not suitable for commercial product work under its current research-only terms.
tier_shortlist.~500M: Qwen2.5-0.5B is the strongest balance of context/multilingual use and Apache model license; verify training-data transparency. SmolLM2-360M is a slightly smaller but more reproducibly documented option.
tier_shortlist.~700M: Cerebras-GPT-590M is the nearest verified candidate in this pass (not an exact 700M model); it is Apache-2.0 and unusually well documented, but trained on only 20 tokens per parameter and has 2K context. Qwen2.5-0.5B and Pythia-410M are smaller alternatives.
tier_shortlist.~1B: OLMo-1B for reproducibility/open data/code; Qwen2.5-1.5B if a larger, longer-context multilingual base is acceptable; Pythia-1B as a controlled research baseline. OpenELM-1.1B is license-blocked for commercial Pocket AI.
tier_shortlist.~1.5–2B: Qwen2.5-1.5B for multilingual/32K context and Apache repository terms; SmolLM2-1.7B is a major candidate that needs full row/license verification before treating as SAFE; Pythia-1.4B provides training reproducibility but is older and English-only.
tier_shortlist.~3–4B: Pythia-2.8B is the clearest permissive documented foundation in current rows; Qwen2.5-3B has excellent context but research-only license; OpenELM-3B is research-only. No one overall winner.

method_limitations: This is a systematic representative shortlist, not an exhaustive inventory of every Hub repository. Search results identify some additional size families (e.g. Cerebras-GPT and MobileLLM); they require individual license-file and artifact verification before inclusion. Unknown means not verified from the primary source reviewed. Benchmark fields point to documented author evaluations rather than inventing precise scores. Suitability labels are screening flags, not legal advice.
